But while the US President says Israel is “very happy” with the agreement, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has yet to publicly endorse it. articles.title: France Cricket implodes: letters hidden in a drawer and a board at war
articles.description: France Cricket's chairman appears to have kept the sports ministry's letters – confirming the body had lost government recognition – from his own board, which is now in revolt. The International Cricket Council has since placed France Cricket on notice and frozen its funding. Yet even as it faces suspension from world cricket, its vice-president just won a seat on the ICC board.

articles.description: Almost all of the tens of thousands of migrants who entered Spain’s enclave of Ceuta had left by Saturday, according to officials. An estimated 60,000 migrants crossed into Ceuta from neighbouring Morocco over just a few days, with at least 67 people losing their lives in the attempt. Spain has announced plans to install a 500-metre-long containment barrier along the sea border, while a majority of EU countries have called for emergency talks in an open letter to the bloc’s interior ministers. articles.title: Africa: Fighting erupts in Ethiopia's Tigray
articles.description: Clashes between Tigray’s TPLF and the Ethiopian federal army are taking place in a contested area of the northern region, with fears of a renewed war. The last Tigray war, which took place between 2020-2022 left 600,000 dead, and the region has not yet recovered. But mediation attempts from the US and African Union have seemingly failed to prevent the worst. Our correspondent in Addis Ababa Tom Canetti with more.

articles.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : Kiev revendique des bombardements contre trois raffineries russes
articles.description: Volodymyr Zelensky a précisé que les raffineries se situaient à près de 1 600 kilomètres des positions ukrainiennes. Plus tôt dans la journée, le chef de la République de Bachkortostan, Radi Khabirov, avait dit avoir « repoussé une nouvelle attaque de drone » contre la ville d’Oufa.

articles.title: Un navire de l'agence atomique russe Rosatom coulé par des drones ukrainiens en mer Noire
articles.description: La Russie et l'Ukraine ont mené ces dernières semaines de nombreuses frappes sur des navires cargo civils en mer Noire, mettant en question la navigation au large des ports russes et ukrainiens.

articles.title: EN DIRECT - Conflit Iran-États-Unis : des ambassades américaines appellent leurs citoyens à «envisager de quitter» le Moyen-Orient
articles.description: «Les Américains présents dans la région devraient envisager de partir, ou être prêts à partir en cas d’escalade», indique une alerte de sécurité dont des versions ont été publiées sur les réseaux sociaux par les missions américaines à Amman, Jérusalem et Bagdad.

articles.title: France's largest wildfire in decades now 'under control', interior minister says
articles.description: French Interior Minister Laurent Nunez on Saturday said that France's largest wildfire since 1949 was "under control", more than a week since the fire erupted in the Gironde department near the southwestern city of Bordeaux. France has for weeks been battling wildfires after a series of deadly heatwaves, which scientists have linked to human-made climate change.

articles.title: Après l'interruption du concert de Barbara Butch, la ministre de la Culture veut renforcer les sanctions contre le délit d'entrave culturel
articles.description: "Ceux qui empêchent un concert de se tenir peuvent s'attendre à des sanctions", a déclaré Catherine Pégard en rappelant que "le délit d'entrave à un spectacle existe".

articles.title: Greece fights fires near Athens
articles.description: Evacuation orders were issued on Friday for areas west and northwest of Athens, as new wildfires broke out near the Greek capital. Firefighters battled to contain the flames, but winds of around 50 miles per hour hampered efforts by water-bombing aircraft. Meanwhile, fires in other parts of the country were brought under control, although the risk of new outbreaks remains very high.

articles.title: West Bank: Settler violence hits "all-time high"
articles.description: Locals in the West Bank say Israeli forces shot and wounded at least one Palestinian and arrested three others on Friday, as they protected Israeli settlers marching through a number of villages. One focal point was the village of Tell, near Nablus in the northern West Bank. Israeli troops sealed off the village on Friday, after carrying out near-daily raids and arrests there since last weekend. Peter O’Brien has more.

articles.title: At least 9 dead, 28 wounded in Kyiv after Russian strikes
articles.description: At leased nine people were killed and 28 others wounded in Ukraine's capital Kyiv after Russia launched a series of ballistic missiles overnight into Saturday, authorities said. Both Russia and Ukraine have ramped up attacks in recent months, with Moscow increasing its long-range strikes on towns and cities across Ukraine. France 24 correspondent Emmanuelle Chaze reports the latest from Kyiv.

articles.title: FIFA President Gianni Infantino scraps controversial World Cup investment plan
articles.description: FIFA President Gianni Infantino was met with unprecedented backlash following his proposal for the structural reform of the World Cup. Under pressure, he announced that he was withdrawing his plan to sell part of the tournament to private investors. This proposal caused quite a stir internally and even led some members of his team to resign in protest.

articles.title: Middle East live: Kuwait says it destroyed hostile Iranian drones targeting vital facilities
articles.description: Kuwait's army on Saturday said it had destroyed hostile Iranian drones ‌in the country's airspace, in what it described as an attack targeting ‌several vital facilities in the country. A government facility ‌in northern Kuwait and a civilian property were hit, the army said, but no casualties were reported. Follow our liveblog for the latest updates.

articles.description: This week several African nations are meeting in Kampala to discuss the future of the African Union Support and Stabilisation Mission in Somalia (AUSSOM). The US announced it will withdraw its funding from the mission which has the objective of fighting against Al Shabab, at the end of this year, putting into question how and if regional forces will be able to proceed. Our correspondent Tom Canetti is in the Somali region and spoke to a refugee who was displaced after Al Shabaab came to his Soma

articles.title: The Dartmouth Workshop: The $7,500 investment that gave birth to AI (2/2)
articles.description: Some 70 years before the current frenzy of record-breaking fundraising by modern AI giants such as OpenAI and Anthropic, the Rockefeller Foundation made what may have been the first investment in the history of AI. With a $7,500 grant from the foundation in 1956, four eminent mathematicians organised The Dartmouth Workshop, where the term “artificial intelligence” was first coined.

articles.title: Décret anti-étrangers en Argentine : en difficulté, Javier Milei tente de se replacer au centre de la scène politique

articles.title: Mort de 67 migrants, l’Espagne sous pression, espace Schengen... Ce que l’on sait de la vague migratoire à Ceuta
articles.description: L’afflux de dizaines de milliers de migrants dans l’enclave espagnole de Ceuta sur la côte nord du Maroc a suscité de nombreuses réactions en Espagne comme à l’étranger. La crise est déjà devenue bien plus qu’un simple épisode migratoire.

articles.title: "C’était une mer de migrants" : traumatisée, Ceuta reprend son souffle après que la plupart des candidats à l'émigration est repartie
articles.description: Au lendemain d'un afflux migratoire sans précédent, la tension reste vive à Ceuta, malgré les dizaines de milliers de retours vers le Maroc. La ville reste profondément marquée. Les commerces ouvrent timidement leurs portes et les habitants recommencent à sortir.
